prompt: This is a New Zealand Electoral Commission party donations and loans return. The declaration page states Parts A, C, D, F and G and a grand total. Part A itemises donations above the disclosure threshold and is the ONLY part carrying donor names; Part G is the aggregate of everything under it and Part F is donations protected from disclosure by law, so neither names anybody. Figures are often typed with no dollar sign and no cents (15,983), and NIL is written for zero. The threshold printed on the line ('of more than $1,500') is the FORM'S text, never the filed amount. Three versions of the grand total exist: (A+C+D+F+G) current with B excluded, (A+C+D+E) intermediate, and (A+B+C+D+E) on the 2019 form where B is anonymous donations and IS summed.
notes: Learned across C417/C438/C441-C447, 2026-09-23/24. A declared NIL is a COMPLETE return, not a missing one: 13 of the 110 live returns since 2019 declare exactly zero. tables.hazards:
FOUR HAZARDS, all found by Arthur's review of 2026-09-25 and all invisible to a whole-document text test.
  1. A CONTINUATION PAGE. The schedule runs onto a sheet the reader never opens. Green 2023's is numbered 'Page: 6.1' and carries the NINE largest donations in the return ($546,222.92). The stamp sits bottom-right, which is the AMOUNT column of the last row on the page — so the last row of each page of a stamped return is the one to check.

by: claude
title: Default extraction — a document nothing recognises
applies_to: Any document no type profile recognises. It is not a fallback in the sense of a lesser reading: it is the STATED extraction for an unknown document, so that what happens to a new file is a decision somebody can read rather than whatever the calling lane happened to do.

tooling.parse: none — the default reads TEXT, it does not claim a structure

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80
config.cache: by document sha; a page image is immutable, so its reading is too
config.prompt: the bare instruction 'OCR' — the model is a TRANSCRIBER

process: 1. Identify the document by the sha256 of its bytes, never by filename.
2. Measure its surface: pages, characters per page, producer, longest run of text-less pages. This costs no model call and is what a person needs to write the profile that would have matched.
3. Read the text layer with pdftotext -layout.
4. Recognise every page whose text layer holds under 80 characters, and splice those readings into the text layer in page order.
5. Record which pages were recognised and which could not be read.
6. Stop. The default extracts TEXT and makes no claim about tables, totals or entities — those are a type profile's job.
gates: A page the recogniser failed on is OMITTED and NAMED, never returned empty: an empty page is indistinguishable from a page with nothing on it, and that is how a return reconciles by losing its rows.
A document read to nothing is recorded UNREAD. It is never recorded as a document that said nothing.
on_fail: Record the document unread, with the reason and the pages, and raise it in the document reviewer. Nothing is guessed and no second reader is tried, because there is no second reader.

ocr.notes: The estate's one recogniser. There is nothing behind it.

tables.strategy: none — the default makes no structural claim

prompt: OCR
notes: THE POINT OF A DEFAULT is that an unknown document has a stated reading. Before 2026-09-25 it had whatever the lane that happened to open it did: the party expense returns were read by a local OCR engine for a day because the lane called it directly, while the estate's chosen recogniser sat running on both boxes. A profile is where that decision lives now.

by: claude
title: EC party ELECTION EXPENSES return — what a party spent
applies_to: A registered party's return of election expenses for a general election (Electoral Act 1993 s 206I). 40 held for 2020 and 2023. NOT a donations return and never summed with one: this is money SPENT, the other is money received.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --party-expenses (the Commission's own summary page per election, captured)

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80

process: 1. Read the Commission's summary table for the election: limit, total expenses, broadcasting allocation, allocation spent, audited.
2. Take the FIRST document the table links for the party — where a return was amended the page lists the amendment first, and an amendment supersedes.
3. Read the document's text layer. If it states a total, that is the reading.
4. Otherwise recognise every page and read the same patterns over the result.
5. A person's reading, recorded in expense_readings.jsonl, outranks both.
gates: THE FORM BEATS THE AUDITOR. `Total (A + B + C)` is the party's own declaration; `Total Party Election Expenses:` is the auditor's report attached to it. TOP's amended 2023 return contradicts itself because the amendment was filed without re-issuing the report.
PART D IS NOT AN ELECTION EXPENSE. It is the broadcasting allocation spend, published in its own column. Summing every 'TOTAL FOR PART' line adds $1,248,924.19 to Labour's 2020 campaign.
A PARTIAL SET OF PARTS IS NOT A TOTAL. The form prints all three, $0.00 included, so a reading holding two has missed one.
THE FORM'S OWN ARITHMETIC. Where a reading has both a stated total and the parts, they must agree to the dollar.
THE LIMIT PRINTED ON THE FORM bounds the reading. Spending over it is an offence, so a figure above it is a misread or the story of the decade.
NIL IS A FIGURE (0.00); N/A IS NOT (NULL).
on_fail: The Commission's published figure stands, the row records why the document could not be read, and the document goes to the reviewer. A recognised reading that DISAGREES with the Commission is treated as the suspect; a text-layer or human reading that disagrees is published over the Commission (Māori Party 2020).

ocr.notes: 21 of the 40 have no text layer or print the declaration page as an image.

tables.strategy: not a table — four labelled figures on a declaration page, plus TOTAL FOR PART lines on the schedules
tables.notes: The itemised schedules behind them name the SUPPLIER on every line. That is a register this estate does not have and should; it is separate work.

prompt: This is a New Zealand Electoral Commission party ELECTION EXPENSES return. The declaration page states Part A (advertisements promoted solely by the party), Part B (shared with candidates), Part C (authorised and promoted by a third party) and their total, then Parts D to F, which are the BROADCASTING ALLOCATION and are a different figure entirely. Return the figures as printed; do not compute a total the form does not print.
notes: Built 2026-09-25 (ruling 351). Reading these found the Commission's own summary table wrong twice: Māori Party 2020 publishes Part A alone ($241,986.42) against the return's declared $301,517.96, and TOP's 2023 amended return contradicts itself.

by: claude
title: EC party ANNUAL FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
applies_to: A registered party's annual financial statements (Electoral Act 1993 ss 210F–210J; financial years from 2023, filed within six months of balance date). 46 held, all 2024. Not donations and not expenses: a balance sheet and a statement of financial performance.

tooling.read: ops/ec_financials_read.py (LLM page-read, cited to the document)

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80

process: 1. Hold the document: file, sha, source URL, pages, the party it resolves to and on what basis.
2. Read its text layer; recognise the pages that have none.
3. Take the headline figures from the document's own text, one row per figure, each cited to the document.
gates: `-layout` IS LOAD-BEARING. Without it poppler de-columnises the table and a label lands on a different line from its figure: Labour's 2026 statement reached the reader as `Total Assets` alone.
NOTHING IS SUMMED ACROSS DOCUMENTS. A figure the text does not state is ABSENT, never zero.
THE PRIOR-YEAR COLUMN IS NOT THIS YEAR. These statements print two columns and three page-reads have already reported the wrong one.
on_fail: The figure is absent and the page says so.

tables.strategy: layout-preserved text, label and figure on one line
tables.notes: Two columns: current year and prior year.

prompt: These are a New Zealand political party's annual financial statements. Two columns of figures are printed: the financial year being reported and the PRIOR year. Return only the reported year's figures and say which year that is. Do not compute any figure the statement does not print.
notes: C364. Held from 2024 only; nothing for 2019–2023.

by: claude
title: Quarterly expenses workbook — MPs and members of the Executive
applies_to: The quarterly expense disclosures published proactively by Parliamentary Service (members) and the Department of Internal Affairs (members of the Executive). 31 + 69 held. A SPREADSHEET, not a document: no page, no text layer, no recogniser.

tooling.read: openpyxl / xlrd — the workbook is read as cells, never rendered

config.pages: none — this is not a page format

process: 1. Find the header row by its known column labels, not by position: the workbook carries a title row above it and the row moves.
2. Skip the PARTY HEADING rows (National / Act / NZ First …) — they are section headers, not members.
3. One row per member per quarter, each figure by column NAME.
gates: NO RECOGNISER RUNS ON A SPREADSHEET. A profile that named one would be describing work that never happens.
A COLUMN IS FOUND BY ITS LABEL. These workbooks change column order between quarters and a positional read files the wrong money under the wrong heading — the failure class C403 exists for.
on_fail: The quarter loads no rows and says which file and which header it could not find.

ocr.notes: A spreadsheet has no pixels to read.

tables.strategy: cells, by column label

notes: Two publishers, one shape, deliberately one profile: the DIA workbook is the Parliamentary Service workbook with the Executive's own columns added (C379).

by: claude
title: Captured web page — a site's own page, printed to PDF
applies_to: A page captured from an organisation's website by the whole-site crawl (ruling 180), stored under a content hash rather than a title. 344 held from the party sites. The bytes are a PDF; the DOCUMENT is a web page, and its authority is the site's, not a filing's.

config.pages: pages with no text layer

process: 1. The capture records the URL, the fetch time and the robots decision that permitted it.
2. Read the text layer — a printed page almost always has one.
3. Recognise only the pages that do not.
gates: A PAGE IS NOT A FILING. Nothing read here is a register row; it is an organisation's own assertion about itself, and it is tiered as one.
THE CAPTURE'S ROBOTS DECISION TRAVELS WITH IT. A page collected under the government proactive-release exemption (ruling 242) is marked so.
on_fail: The page is held unread; a site page is re-fetchable, so an unread one is a re-capture and not a loss.

ocr.notes: Rare: a printed page carries its own text.

tables.strategy: none by default

prompt: This is a page from an organisation's own website, captured as a PDF. Anything it asserts is that organisation's claim about itself.
notes: Filenames are content hashes, so `filename_any` can never recognise one — the producer signal can, and that is the case the signals block exists for.

by: claude
title: EC party ELECTION EXPENSES return — what a party spent
applies_to: A registered party's return of election expenses for a general election (Electoral Act 1993 s 206I). 40 held for 2020 and 2023. NOT a donations return and never summed with one: this is money SPENT, the other is money received.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --party-expenses (the Commission's own summary page per election, captured)

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80

process: 1. Read the Commission's summary table for the election: limit, total expenses, broadcasting allocation, allocation spent, audited.
2. Take the FIRST document the table links for the party — where a return was amended the page lists the amendment first, and an amendment supersedes.
3. Read the document's text layer. If it states a total, that is the reading.
4. Otherwise recognise every page and read the same patterns over the result.

5. Take the parts from BOTH places the form prints them: `TOTAL FOR PART A` at the foot of each schedule, and the `Part A: … $x` lines in the declaration block on page 1. The schedule is preferred where both read. A return whose schedules will not recognise can still be checked against its own arithmetic this way — which is how Advance NZ 2020 was settled.
6. A person's reading, recorded in expense_readings.jsonl, outranks both.
gates: THE FORM BEATS THE AUDITOR. `Total (A + B + C)` is the party's own declaration; `Total Party Election Expenses:` is the auditor's report attached to it. TOP's amended 2023 return contradicts itself because the amendment was filed without re-issuing the report.
PART D IS NOT AN ELECTION EXPENSE. It is the broadcasting allocation spend, published in its own column. Summing every 'TOTAL FOR PART' line adds $1,248,924.19 to Labour's 2020 campaign.
A PARTIAL SET OF PARTS IS NOT A TOTAL. The form prints all three, $0.00 included, so a reading holding two has missed one.
THE FORM'S OWN ARITHMETIC. Where a reading has both a stated total and the parts, they must agree to the dollar. This is what refuses a recognised total whose characters are individually plausible.
THE LIMIT PRINTED ON THE FORM bounds the reading. Spending over it is an offence, so a figure above it is a misread or the story of the decade.
NIL IS A FIGURE (0.00); N/A IS NOT (NULL).

A PART TOTAL MAY BE PRINTED WITH NO DOLLAR SIGN. NZ Loyal 2023 prints `TOTAL FOR PART A 300476.58`, and a greedy gap between the label and the figure read it as $6.58 — 99.998% short, with nothing about it looking wrong. The gap is lazy AND guarded by a lookbehind; lazy alone still starts at the first digit it can reach.

THE COMMISSION'S PUBLISHED TOTAL IS A READING TOO, and it can be wrong the same way twice. Its 2020 table publishes PART A ALONE as the total for the Māori Party ($241,986.42 against a declared $301,517.96) and for Advance NZ ($364,769.96 against a declared $403,583.95). Check a published total against the form's own parts before treating the publisher as the authority.
on_fail: The Commission's published figure stands, the row records why the document could not be read, and the document goes to the reviewer. Where a reading DISAGREES with the Commission the rule turns on what corroborates it: a text-layer or human reading is published over the table; a recognised reading is published only if the document's own parts add to its own total (`stated_consistent`), because four separately printed figures agreeing is not a guess about characters. A recognised reading nothing corroborates leaves the Commission's figure standing and goes to review — which is where NZ Loyal's 2023 amendment sits, a 6 most likely read as an 8.

ocr.notes: 21 of the 40 have no text layer or print the declaration page as an image.

tables.strategy: not a table — four labelled figures on a declaration page, plus TOTAL FOR PART lines on the schedules
tables.notes: The itemised schedules behind them name the SUPPLIER on every line. That is a register this estate does not have and should; it is separate work.

prompt: This is a New Zealand Electoral Commission party ELECTION EXPENSES return. The declaration page states Part A (advertisements promoted solely by the party), Part B (shared with candidates), Part C (authorised and promoted by a third party) and their total, then Parts D to F, which are the BROADCASTING ALLOCATION and are a different figure entirely. Return the figures as printed; do not compute a total the form does not print.
notes: Built 2026-09-25 (ruling 351) and re-read the same day with GLM-OCR after Arthur removed the local OCR engine from the estate. 35 of 37 rows read from the document, 32 agreeing with the Commission to the cent; 16 of 16 for the eight front-page parties, who spent $19,603,557.76. Reading the returns found the Commission's own table wrong three times: Māori Party 2020 and Advance NZ 2020 published as Part A alone, and TOP's 2023 amended return contradicting itself. Two remain unread — ALCP 2023 ($986.00) and Democratic Alliance 2023 (NIL) — and both are in the reviewer. The itemised schedules behind these declarations name the SUPPLIER on every line; that is a register this estate does not have and should, and it is separate work.

by: claude
title: Default extraction — a document nothing recognises
applies_to: Any document no type profile recognises. It is not a fallback in the sense of a lesser reading: it is the STATED extraction for an unknown document, so that what happens to a new file is a decision somebody can read rather than whatever the calling lane happened to do.

tooling.parse: none — the default reads TEXT, it does not claim a structure

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80
config.cache: by document sha; a page image is immutable, so its reading is too
config.prompt: the bare instruction 'OCR' — the model is a TRANSCRIBER

process: 1. Identify the document by the sha256 of its bytes, never by filename.
2. Measure its surface: pages, characters per page, producer, longest run of text-less pages. This costs no model call and is what a person needs to write the profile that would have matched.
3. Read the text layer with pdftotext -layout.
4. Recognise every page whose text layer holds under 80 characters, and splice those readings into the text layer in page order.
5. Record which pages were recognised and which could not be read.
6. Stop. The default extracts TEXT and makes no claim about tables, totals or entities — those are a type profile's job.
gates: A page the recogniser failed on is OMITTED and NAMED, never returned empty: an empty page is indistinguishable from a page with nothing on it, and that is how a return reconciles by losing its rows.
A document read to nothing is recorded UNREAD. It is never recorded as a document that said nothing.

A GAP BETWEEN A LABEL AND ITS FIGURE MUST BE LAZY AND GUARDED. A pattern that skips 'whatever is between' and then matches a number will start the number as late as it can: `TOTAL FOR PART A 300476.58` matched as $6.58 because the gap ate `30047`. Lazy alone is not enough — a lookbehind must stop the match beginning mid-number.

A PUBLISHED SUMMARY OF A DOCUMENT IS A READING, NOT THE DOCUMENT. Where a publisher states a figure the document also states, check one against the other; the Electoral Commission's 2020 expenses table is wrong about two parties in the same way, and no amount of internal consistency checking would have found it.

TWO READERS DISAGREEING IS THE CHEAPEST DEFECT DETECTOR THIS ESTATE HAS. Both of today's reader bugs — a dollar sign read as a 9, and a greedy gap eating five digits — surfaced because something else read the same page and the answers differed. Neither was visible in its own output.
on_fail: Record the document unread, with the reason and the pages, and raise it in the document reviewer. Nothing is guessed and no second reader is tried, because there is no second reader.

ocr.notes: The estate's one recogniser. There is nothing behind it.

tables.strategy: none — the default makes no structural claim

prompt: OCR
notes:
THE POINT OF A DEFAULT is that an unknown document has a stated reading. Before 2026-09-25 it had whatever the lane that happened to open it did: the party expense returns were read by a local OCR engine for a day because the lane called it directly, while the estate's chosen recogniser sat running on both boxes. A profile is where that decision lives now.

Revised 2026-09-25 after the party expense returns: the gates added here are the ones that are about READING ANY DOCUMENT rather than about that form, so the next type profile inherits them by being read beside this one.

by: claude
title: EC party return — no text layer at all, a photograph of paper

ocr.notes: ONE RECOGNISER, AND NOTHING BEHIND IT. Measured over the 84 staged returns with no text layer: GLM-OCR parses a page-1 total on 28 that the local engine retired on 2026-09-25 could not, that engine parsed NONE GLM could not, and on the single disagreement it was wrong (TEA Party 2020: $619.77 read off a page saying 'Total (A + C + D + F + G) = 154,619.77'). A first sighting has no prior row for READER_RANK to defend, so a weaker figure would land unchallenged — which is how 'Chaistopher Yaakin' $820,500 reached a person's page. A scan this reader cannot read is recorded UNPARSED and the page says so.

tables.strategy: geometry, not the transcriber
tables.notes: docread's trust policy: DONOR cells to the transcriber, STRUCTURE to geometry, because each mangles what the other reads. The geometry reader's bands can OVERLAP, which emits one donation two and three times (C433) — check a part's rows against its own printed TOTAL FOR PART before trusting them.
tables.reconcile: THE RETURN CHECKS ITSELF. Every EC return prints TOTAL FOR PART A on its first schedule page. A complete reading of Part A sums to it, and a reading that does not is INCOMPLETE OR WRONG — not a return with missing donors. All five reading failures found on 2026-09-25 were visible this way on the day they were made, and none was noticed, because the rows were published without the check. Reconcile before you publish; where it fails, ask a person.
tables.hazards:
FOUR HAZARDS, all found by Arthur's review of 2026-09-25 and all invisible to a whole-document text test.
  1. A CONTINUATION PAGE. The schedule runs onto a sheet the reader never opens. Green 2023's is numbered 'Page: 6.1' and carries the NINE largest donations in the return ($546,222.92). NZ First 2024's says so on its own face — 'Page added at the request of the Electoral commision due to space constraints in date feild of main form'. Look for a printed page label with a decimal, and for a sheet between two consecutively numbered pages.
  2. A CONTINUATION PAGE IS NOT A SCHEDULE. NZ First 2024's inserted sheet is a DATE BREAKDOWN whose last column is 'Donor Total' — the same figure already on the main form. Read as a schedule it produces duplicate donations; the reader took four of its detail lines as the donors' amounts and lost $89,921.04.
  3. AN AUDITOR'S STAMP OVER A FIGURE. Labour 2020 row 11 is $40,020.00 printed under Grant Thornton's circular 'Marked for identification purposes', and came back as $460.00. The stamp sits bottom-right, which is the AMOUNT column of the last row on the page — so the last row of each page of a stamped return is the one to check.
  4. A TWO-COLUMN DONOR CELL. Some forms put the donor's NAME and their STREET ADDRESS in separate table columns under one 'Donor's name and street address' heading. Green 2023 does, and the reader took the address column: 49 rows reading '<a donor's street address>' where a person's name belongs. If every donor in a part looks like an address, you are one column to the right.

prompt: This is a New Zealand Electoral Commission party donations and loans return. The DECLARATION page states Parts A, C, D, F and G and a grand total. Part A itemises donations above the disclosure threshold and is the ONLY part carrying donor names; Part G is the aggregate of everything under it and Part F is donations protected from disclosure by law, so neither names anybody — money sitting only in those parts is UNATTRIBUTED, not missing. Figures are often typed with no dollar sign and no cents (15,983), and NIL is written for zero; a declared NIL is a COMPLETE return, not a missing one. The threshold printed on a line ('of more than $1,500') is the FORM'S text and never the filed amount. Three versions of the grand total exist: (A+C+D+F+G) current with B excluded, (A+C+D+E) intermediate, and (A+B+C+D+E) on the 2019 form where B is anonymous donations and IS summed. Donor schedule pages print 'TOTAL FOR PART <X>' at the foot of each part's own table, which is a check on the declaration page.
notes:
9 of the eight parties' 56 live returns are this shape. A scan that yields nothing is recorded UNPARSED and the page says so; a second-rate figure published as a party's declared total is worse than an honest gap.

A scan cannot hide a two-column donor cell or a continuation page — it hides everything equally — so the hazards below matter here most, and the reconciliation check is the only thing that will tell you.

by: claude
title: Electoral Commission — party donations and loans annual return

ocr.pages: page 1, plus the page carrying TOTAL PARTY DONATIONS wherever it is in the first 14
ocr.notes: 84 of 125 staged returns have NO usable text layer, and a text layer is per PAGE: a document can hold 6,000 characters of auditor's report and have an IMAGE for its declaration page (New Conservative 2022, Outdoors and Freedom 2022). Read page 1 alone: under 50 characters means recognise it, whatever the whole document holds. GLM-OCR is the estate's one recogniser and there is nothing behind it.

tables.strategy: ruled border, and the row-number column sits OUTSIDE it
tables.notes: A generative transcriber decides per page whether the outside row-number column is part of the table — National 2017 kept it on page 3 and dropped it on page 2, identical layout, same model, temperature 0. A parser anchored on the row number discards correctly-read rows. GLM also stops before the 'TOTAL FOR PART A' line on some donor pages; a second engine used to splice that line back and was removed on 2026-09-25, so those returns now fail their own reconciliation and go to the reviewer instead — which is the intended trade.

prompt: This is a New Zealand Electoral Commission party donations and loans return. The declaration page states Parts A, C, D, F and G and a grand total. Part A itemises donations above the disclosure threshold and is the ONLY part carrying donor names; Part G is the aggregate of everything under it and Part F is donations protected from disclosure by law, so neither names anybody. Figures are often typed with no dollar sign and no cents (15,983), and NIL is written for zero. The threshold printed on the line ('of more than $1,500') is the FORM'S text, never the filed amount. Three versions of the grand total exist: (A+C+D+F+G) current with B excluded, (A+C+D+E) intermediate, and (A+B+C+D+E) on the 2019 form where B is anonymous donations and IS summed.
notes:
RETIRED 2026-09-24, superseded by the three SHAPE profiles — `ec-party-return-text`, `-image-declaration`, `-scan`. This one recognised the family but carried one reading plan for three different documents, and the difference between them is the whole problem: a text-layer filing must NOT be recognised, a scan must be recognised entirely, and the commonest shape of all needs page 1 recognised and spliced onto its own text layer. Retired the way this store retires anything — a new version with no recognition rules, which matches nothing — so every word of what it knew stays readable in its history.

Learned across C417/C438/C441-C447, 2026-09-23/24. A declared NIL is a COMPLETE return, not a missing one: 13 of the 110 live returns since 2019 declare exactly zero. The EC publishes the original and every amendment as separate files, and the same return sits in two staging trees under different names, so identity is the sha256. An `-audited` filing may be the auditor's report WITH the declaration as an image page 1 — do not conclude it holds no return from the text layer.

by: claude
applies_to: An electorate candidate's return of election expenses — Parts F and G of the candidate return of donations, expenses and loans (Electoral Act 1993 s 205K). 1,065 held for 2020 and 2023. It is the SAME DOCUMENT as the candidate donations return and a different READING of it: the donations reading is frozen and this pass may not touch it.

tooling.serve: query.influence.browse (the electorate map's shading is the Commission's index, not this)

config.pages: only the pages whose own text carries an expense label

process: Page texts come from the same extractor the chunked reader uses; a scan's OCR is already cached, so the saving is model calls and not pages.
Only pages matching an expense label are sent. A twelve-page return costs three calls, not thirteen.
Each figure is taken ONLY from a page printing its own label, so a later $0.00 part total cannot overwrite a real figure.

The DECLARATION BLOCK on page 1 states the same three heads as the schedule pages and is read as well, because a return whose schedule pages will not recognise can still be checked against its own arithmetic.
The expense fields are REQUIRED in the response schema. An optional field in a json_schema is a field the model will omit — that is why 1,674 readings carried a null total.
gates: THE FORM'S OWN ARITHMETIC: F + G must make the stated total. NULL where the form gives too little to check — a total with no parts, or no total — which is neither a pass nor a failure.

A GATE THAT CANNOT FAIL IS NOT A GATE. The arithmetic above passes every empty reading, because 0 + 0 makes 0. Seven scanned returns read NIL against a Commission figure and every one of them passed it.

A FIGURE IS NOT ALWAYS BESIDE ITS LABEL, and on this form family it is the normal case. These are fillable PDFs: the value a filer types lands where the WIDGET sits, which is not the line the label prints on. Make It Legal's Part B total prints three lines above `TOTAL FOR PART B`; Diana Burgess's candidate total prints on the line `Write 'NIL' if you have NO expenses to declare`. A same-line rule reads both returns as declaring nothing, and the second one PASSED the form's own arithmetic because the parts it did find were 0 and 0 + 0 makes 0.

A ZERO IS NOT BELIEVED OVER A LARGER NUMBER ON THE SAME DOCUMENT. `missed_total` asks whether SECTION 3 OF THE DECLARATION PAGE prints a figure larger than everything the reader claimed; if it does the reading is refused, not published as nil.

THE SECTION, NOT THE PAGE. Page 1 declares donations, expenses and loans one after another, so a check over the whole page reads `Part A: Candidate donations of more than $1,500` as a missed expense. A check over every page reads `Flier: 30 September to 10,000 households` the same way.
The form's printed THRESHOLDS and CAPS are the form talking about money, not a candidate declaring it, and are blanked before a line is searched.
NIL IS A FIGURE. A candidate who declared nothing spent nothing and loads as 0.00, never NULL.
on_fail: The reading is recorded with the reason and `expenses_consistent` is NULL; the Commission's index figure stands as the published one and the disagreement is reported per candidate. Abstain is the design — a refused reading is never replaced by a weaker instrument's.
notes: WRITTEN 2026-09-26, AFTER THE FACT AND THAT IS THE DEFECT. This reading was built, debugged through three false-positive storms and shipped before anyone asked which profile it belonged to, so the form's structure lived as loose regexes in a reader and the displaced-figure rule was solved TWICE in one day in two modules that do not know about each other — `registers.promoters._figure_near` and `ec_pageread.read.missed_total`. The profile is where a fact about a form family belongs.

by: claude
applies_to: A registered promoter's return of election expenses — a third party, neither party nor candidate, that spent over $100,000 on election advertising (Electoral Act 1993 s 206ZC). 20 of 21 held for 2020 and 2023.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --promoters (the Commission's expense page, which STATES each figure)

config.pages: every page, the longest held return being 8

process: The Commission's own expense page states every figure, so the document read has a gate before it is taken.
The SCHEDULE's `TOTAL FOR PART X` beats the DECLARATION block where both read: the schedule total is the figure the itemised rows add to.
Eleven of the twenty held returns have no text layer and are read by the recogniser; the reading is cached by sha256, never by filename.
gates: THE THREE HEADS OF 2020 ARE NOT ADDITIVE AND ARE NEVER SUMMED ACROSS A ROW. The form counts an advertisement that is both an election and a referendum advertisement IN FULL under each head. Family First declared $141,224.34 under Parts A, B and C and spent it once; a row sum publishes $423,673.02 that nobody spent.
PART A IS THE PUBLISHED FIGURE. It is money spent to influence a vote for a party or candidate. Referendum advertising bought a referendum result and is carried beside it, never inside it.
2023 RAN NO REFERENDUM, so its Parts B and C are NULL and not 0.00 — the head did not exist, which is a different statement from declaring nothing under it.

A FIGURE IS NOT ALWAYS BESIDE ITS LABEL, and on this form family it is the normal case. These are fillable PDFs: the value a filer types lands where the WIDGET sits, which is not the line the label prints on. Make It Legal's Part B total prints three lines above `TOTAL FOR PART B`; Diana Burgess's candidate total prints on the line `Write 'NIL' if you have NO expenses to declare`. A same-line rule reads both returns as declaring nothing, and the second one PASSED the form's own arithmetic because the parts it did find were 0 and 0 + 0 makes 0.

The form's printed THRESHOLD ($100,000 to file) and CAP are blanked before a line is searched for money. The Public Service Association's NIL return read $100,000 under all three heads, consistent with itself, until they were.
NIL IS A FIGURE and an empty cell is not one. The Commission writes Nil; a blank cell holds nothing to read.
on_fail: The Commission's stated figure loads and `stated_*` stays NULL with the reason. A promoter whose return is not held at all (The Better NZ Trust, 403 twice, ledgered) still carries the Commission's figure, because dropping a figure for want of its document is how 56 donation returns went missing.
notes: The register page is a DOCUMENT in its own right and has no asset to download: the promoters, their representatives, their directors and their trustees are the page's own body, held as rendered HTML under `promoter-register__<year>.html`. 249 named people come from it, and it is the only source in this estate tying an election spender that is neither party nor candidate to persons.

by: claude
title: EC party ELECTION EXPENSES return — what a party spent
applies_to: A registered party's return of election expenses for a general election (Electoral Act 1993 s 206I). 40 held for 2020 and 2023. NOT a donations return and never summed with one: this is money SPENT, the other is money received.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --party-expenses (the Commission's own summary page per election, captured)

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80

process: 1. Read the Commission's summary table for the election: limit, total expenses, broadcasting allocation, allocation spent, audited.
2. Take the FIRST document the table links for the party — where a return was amended the page lists the amendment first, and an amendment supersedes.
3. Read the document's text layer. If it states a total, that is the reading.
4. Otherwise recognise every page and read the same patterns over the result.

5. Take the parts from BOTH places the form prints them: `TOTAL FOR PART A` at the foot of each schedule, and the `Part A: … $x` lines in the declaration block on page 1. The schedule is preferred where both read. A return whose schedules will not recognise can still be checked against its own arithmetic this way — which is how Advance NZ 2020 was settled.
6. A person's reading, recorded in expense_readings.jsonl, outranks both.
gates: THE FORM BEATS THE AUDITOR. `Total (A + B + C)` is the party's own declaration; `Total Party Election Expenses:` is the auditor's report attached to it. TOP's amended 2023 return contradicts itself because the amendment was filed without re-issuing the report.
PART D IS NOT AN ELECTION EXPENSE. It is the broadcasting allocation spend, published in its own column. Summing every 'TOTAL FOR PART' line adds $1,248,924.19 to Labour's 2020 campaign.
A PARTIAL SET OF PARTS IS NOT A TOTAL. The form prints all three, $0.00 included, so a reading holding two has missed one.
THE FORM'S OWN ARITHMETIC. Where a reading has both a stated total and the parts, they must agree to the dollar. This is what refuses a recognised total whose characters are individually plausible.
THE LIMIT PRINTED ON THE FORM bounds the reading. Spending over it is an offence, so a figure above it is a misread or the story of the decade.
NIL IS A FIGURE (0.00); N/A IS NOT (NULL).

A PART TOTAL MAY BE PRINTED WITH NO DOLLAR SIGN. NZ Loyal 2023 prints `TOTAL FOR PART A 300476.58`, and a greedy gap between the label and the figure read it as $6.58 — 99.998% short, with nothing about it looking wrong. The gap is lazy AND guarded by a lookbehind; lazy alone still starts at the first digit it can reach.

THE COMMISSION'S PUBLISHED TOTAL IS A READING TOO, and it can be wrong the same way twice. Its 2020 table publishes PART A ALONE as the total for the Māori Party ($241,986.42 against a declared $301,517.96) and for Advance NZ ($364,769.96 against a declared $403,583.95). Check a published total against the form's own parts before treating the publisher as the authority.
on_fail: The Commission's published figure stands, the row records why the document could not be read, and the document goes to the reviewer. WHERE A READING DISAGREES WITH THE COMMISSION, THE COMMISSION'S FIGURE IS STILL THE ONE PUBLISHED (Arthur, 2026-09-27: "I've changed my mind. the comission should have the headline number. It should have a hyperlink to the comissions page that shows the number"), with our reading published beside it and the row tagged `spent_unreconciled` — neither is corrected to the other. This SUPERSEDES version 2, which published a text-layer or human reading over the table and a recognised reading over it where the document's own parts added to its own total (`stated_consistent`). That rule is still true about the DOCUMENTS — the Māori Party's 2020 return declares $301,517.96 against the Commission's $241,986.42, which is Part A alone — and `stated_consistent` is still read and still stated; what changed is which figure carries the headline. `query.influence.donations._spent` is the one implementation.

ocr.notes: 21 of the 40 have no text layer or print the declaration page as an image.

tables.strategy: not a table — four labelled figures on a declaration page, plus TOTAL FOR PART lines on the schedules
tables.notes: The itemised schedules behind them name the SUPPLIER on every line. That is a register this estate does not have and should; it is separate work.

prompt: This is a New Zealand Electoral Commission party ELECTION EXPENSES return. The declaration page states Part A (advertisements promoted solely by the party), Part B (shared with candidates), Part C (authorised and promoted by a third party) and their total, then Parts D to F, which are the BROADCASTING ALLOCATION and are a different figure entirely. Return the figures as printed; do not compute a total the form does not print.

The itemised schedules behind these declarations name the SUPPLIER on every line; that is a register this estate does not have and should, and it is separate work. | v3 (2026-09-30): on_fail rewritten to the 2026-09-27 ruling. Version 2 had described the superseded publication rule for three days after the code stopped applying it, and the test that was meant to hold the two together was asserting the old rule as well — a profile is how the next document gets read, so a stale one is a live instruction.

title: Default extraction — a document nothing recognises

ocr.notes: The estate's one recogniser. There is nothing behind it.

tables.strategy: none — the default makes no structural claim

prompt: OCR
notes:
THE POINT OF A DEFAULT is that an unknown document has a stated reading. Before 2026-09-25 it had whatever the lane that happened to open it did: the party expense returns were read by a local OCR engine for a day because the lane called it directly, while the estate's chosen recogniser sat running on both boxes. A profile is where that decision lives now.

Revised 2026-09-25 after the party expense returns: the gates added here are the ones that are about READING ANY DOCUMENT rather than about that form, so the next type profile inherits them by being read beside this one. | v3 (2026-10-19): Step 3 verdict under ruling 60 (the trial halted with pass two part-run, 19 October): GLM-OCR Q8_0 under the prompt "OCR" stays the page reader, alone. No challenger reached zero loop or invented-text failures on the pages both read: OvisOCR2 on 2,327 shared pages had 68 loop pages to GLM-OCR's 27 (18 runaways of 100+ repeats to 8); Infinity-Parser2-Pro Q4_K_M on 445 had 24 to 9; Chandra OCR 2 on 191 had 17 to 9; all three read amounts on complete text keys at least as well as the incumbent. No second reader (card no-second-reader-qualifies-under-the-trial-s-rules). 300 dpi over 200 changed nothing measurable on 2,063 shared pages (loop pages 20 to 18, exact amounts 122 to 121 of 139 keys), so the dpi stands as written; f16 over Q8_0 agreed on every amount of the twenty-page comparison. Write-up: docs/trials/page-readers.md.
applies_to: Any document no type profile recognises. It is not a fallback in the sense of a lesser reading: it is the STATED extraction for an unknown document, so that what happens to a new file is a decision somebody can read rather than whatever the calling lane happened to do.

tooling.parse: none — the default reads TEXT, it does not claim a structure

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80
config.cache: by document sha; a page image is immutable, so its reading is too
config.prompt: the bare instruction 'OCR' — the model is a TRANSCRIBER

process: 1. Identify the document by the sha256 of its bytes, never by filename.
2. Measure its surface: pages, characters per page, producer, longest run of text-less pages. This costs no model call and is what a person needs to write the profile that would have matched.
3. Read the text layer with pdftotext -layout.
4. Recognise every page whose text layer holds under 80 characters, and splice those readings into the text layer in page order.
5. Record which pages were recognised and which could not be read.
6. Stop. The default extracts TEXT and makes no claim about tables, totals or entities — those are a type profile's job.
gates: A page the recogniser failed on is OMITTED and NAMED, never returned empty: an empty page is indistinguishable from a page with nothing on it, and that is how a return reconciles by losing its rows.
A document read to nothing is recorded UNREAD. It is never recorded as a document that said nothing.

A GAP BETWEEN A LABEL AND ITS FIGURE MUST BE LAZY AND GUARDED. A pattern that skips 'whatever is between' and then matches a number will start the number as late as it can: `TOTAL FOR PART A 300476.58` matched as $6.58 because the gap ate `30047`. Lazy alone is not enough — a lookbehind must stop the match beginning mid-number.

A PUBLISHED SUMMARY OF A DOCUMENT IS A READING, NOT THE DOCUMENT. Where a publisher states a figure the document also states, check one against the other; the Electoral Commission's 2020 expenses table is wrong about two parties in the same way, and no amount of internal consistency checking would have found it.

TWO READERS DISAGREEING IS THE CHEAPEST DEFECT DETECTOR THIS ESTATE HAS. Both of today's reader bugs — a dollar sign read as a 9, and a greedy gap eating five digits — surfaced because something else read the same page and the answers differed. Neither was visible in its own output.
on_fail: Record the document unread, with the reason and the pages, and raise it in the document reviewer. Nothing is guessed and no second reader is tried, because there is no second reader.

A FIGURE IS NOT ALWAYS BESIDE ITS LABEL, and on this form family it is the normal case. These are fillable PDFs: the value a filer types lands where the WIDGET sits, which is not the line the label prints on. Make It Legal's Part B total prints three lines above `TOTAL FOR PART B`; Diana Burgess's candidate total prints on the line `Write 'NIL' if you have NO expenses to declare`. A same-line rule reads both returns as declaring nothing, and the second one PASSED the form's own arithmetic because the parts it did find were 0 and 0 + 0 makes 0.

A ZERO IS NOT BELIEVED OVER A LARGER NUMBER ON THE SAME DOCUMENT. `missed_total` asks whether SECTION 3 OF THE DECLARATION PAGE prints a figure larger than everything the reader claimed; if it does the reading is refused, not published as nil.

THE SECTION, NOT THE PAGE. Page 1 declares donations, expenses and loans one after another, so a check over the whole page reads `Part A: Candidate donations of more than $1,500` as a missed expense. A check over every page reads `Flier: 30 September to 10,000 households` the same way.
The form's printed THRESHOLDS and CAPS are the form talking about money, not a candidate declaring it, and are blanked before a line is searched.
NIL IS A FIGURE. A candidate who declared nothing spent nothing and loads as 0.00, never NULL.

A RETURN UNDER SEVEN PAGES IS A PARTIAL FILING, NOT A NIL ONE. Six in-window returns are a single scanned declaration page — McCaskey (Kaikōura), Toko (Waikato), Taikato (Bay of Plenty) — with no Part F or G page in the document at all. The reading records `no page of this document prints an expense label` and abstains; the absent parts are NOT zero, and a page count is not a reading.

THE FORM PRINTS THE TOTAL OF F AND G, AND A READER THAT TOOK F AND G HAS ACCOUNTED FOR IT. Section 3 of the declaration page prints four figures — the candidate total, Part F, Part G — and a reader holding F and G has explained the total without ever holding it as a value. Comparing an unattached figure against the PARTS ALONE reported that printed total as money nobody claimed: 17 of this guard's first 24 firings, every one a reading agreeing with the Commission to the cent (Cheung 31,072.85; Bidois 25,708.20; Weenink 25,328.50; Chatterton 23,266.07; Hulman 6,455.33; Allington 3,110.01). The comparison set is `accounted()` — each figure and every SUM of them. A NIL return is unaffected: every subset of 0,0,0 is 0.

NULL IS NOT ZERO, IN THE NOTE AS WELL AS THE FIGURE. Ten of those 17 had no total read at all, and the refusal said `a stated 0.00 is not believed over it` — asserting a declaration the form never made. A return whose total was never read and a return declaring zero are different documents and get different sentences.

A FIELD WHOSE RULE HAS CHANGED MUST BE REWRITTEN BY THE NEW RULE, INCLUDING TO NOTHING. A reading is MERGED into its stored predecessor. Before schema 6 the reader wrote `expenses_unclaimed` only when it found a figure, so values left by an earlier, WIDER rule survived every narrowing: twelve 2023 ACT returns still carried $1,500.00 and $10,000.00 — the DONATIONS threshold and a household count — from a schema that read the whole page. Harmless while only the reader consulted the field in memory; twelve false refusals the moment a re-gate read it back off disk. The reader now always writes the key, and the rule refuses to act on a value stored below schema 6.
on_fail: The reading is recorded with the reason and `expenses_consistent` is NULL; the Commission's index figure stands as the published one and the disagreement is reported per candidate. Abstain is the design — a refused reading is never replaced by a weaker instrument's.

applies_to: A registered party's return of election expenses for a general election (Electoral Act 1993 s 206I). 40 held for 2020 and 2023. NOT a donations return and never summed with one: this is money SPENT, the other is money received.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --party-expenses (the Commission's own summary page per election, captured)

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80

process: 1. Read the Commission's summary table for the election: limit, total expenses, broadcasting allocation, allocation spent, audited.
2. Take the FIRST document the table links for the party — where a return was amended the page lists the amendment first, and an amendment supersedes.
3. Read the document's text layer. If it states a total, that is the reading.
4. Otherwise recognise every page and read the same patterns over the result.

5. Take the parts from BOTH places the form prints them: `TOTAL FOR PART A` at the foot of each schedule, and the `Part A: … $x` lines in the declaration block on page 1. The schedule is preferred where both read. A return whose schedules will not recognise can still be checked against its own arithmetic this way — which is how Advance NZ 2020 was settled.
6. A person's reading, recorded in expense_readings.jsonl, outranks both.
gates: THE FORM BEATS THE AUDITOR. `Total (A + B + C)` is the party's own declaration; `Total Party Election Expenses:` is the auditor's report attached to it. TOP's amended 2023 return contradicts itself because the amendment was filed without re-issuing the report.
PART D IS NOT AN ELECTION EXPENSE. It is the broadcasting allocation spend, published in its own column. Summing every 'TOTAL FOR PART' line adds $1,248,924.19 to Labour's 2020 campaign.
A PARTIAL SET OF PARTS IS NOT A TOTAL. The form prints all three, $0.00 included, so a reading holding two has missed one.
THE FORM'S OWN ARITHMETIC. Where a reading has both a stated total and the parts, they must agree to the dollar. This is what refuses a recognised total whose characters are individually plausible.
THE LIMIT PRINTED ON THE FORM bounds the reading. Spending over it is an offence, so a figure above it is a misread or the story of the decade.
NIL IS A FIGURE (0.00); N/A IS NOT (NULL).

A PART TOTAL MAY BE PRINTED WITH NO DOLLAR SIGN. NZ Loyal 2023 prints `TOTAL FOR PART A 300476.58`, and a greedy gap between the label and the figure read it as $6.58 — 99.998% short, with nothing about it looking wrong. The gap is lazy AND guarded by a lookbehind; lazy alone still starts at the first digit it can reach.

THE COMMISSION'S PUBLISHED TOTAL IS A READING TOO, and it can be wrong the same way twice. Its 2020 table publishes PART A ALONE as the total for the Māori Party ($241,986.42 against a declared $301,517.96) and for Advance NZ ($364,769.96 against a declared $403,583.95). Check a published total against the form's own parts before treating the publisher as the authority.
on_fail: The Commission's published figure stands, the row records why the document could not be read, and the document goes to the reviewer. WHERE A READING DISAGREES WITH THE COMMISSION, THE COMMISSION'S FIGURE IS STILL THE ONE PUBLISHED (Arthur, 2026-09-27: "I've changed my mind. the comission should have the headline number. It should have a hyperlink to the comissions page that shows the number"), with our reading published beside it and the row tagged `spent_unreconciled` — neither is corrected to the other. This SUPERSEDES version 2, which published a text-layer or human reading over the table and a recognised reading over it where the document's own parts added to its own total (`stated_consistent`). That rule is still true about the DOCUMENTS — the Māori Party's 2020 return declares $301,517.96 against the Commission's $241,986.42, which is Part A alone — and `stated_consistent` is still read and still stated; what changed is which figure carries the headline. `query.influence.donations._spent` is the one implementation.

tables.reconcile: THE RETURN CHECKS ITSELF. Every EC return prints TOTAL FOR PART A on its first schedule page. title: EC party return — no text layer at all, a photograph of paper

ocr.notes: ONE RECOGNISER, AND NOTHING BEHIND IT. Measured over the 84 staged returns with no text layer: GLM-OCR parses a page-1 total on 28 that the local engine retired on 2026-09-25 could not, that engine parsed NONE GLM could not, and on the single disagreement it was wrong (TEA Party 2020: $619.77 read off a page saying 'Total (A + C + D + F + G) = 154,619.77'). A first sighting has no prior row for READER_RANK to defend, so a weaker figure would land unchallenged — which is how 'Chaistopher Yaakin' $820,500 reached a person's page. A scan this reader cannot read is recorded UNPARSED and the page says so.

tables.strategy: geometry, not the transcriber
tables.notes: docread's trust policy: DONOR cells to the transcriber, STRUCTURE to geometry, because each mangles what the other reads. The geometry reader's bands can OVERLAP, which emits one donation two and three times (C433) — check a part's rows against its own printed TOTAL FOR PART before trusting them.
tables.reconcile: THE RETURN CHECKS ITSELF. Every EC return prints TOTAL FOR PART A on its first schedule page. A complete reading of Part A sums to it, and a reading that does not is INCOMPLETE OR WRONG — not a return with missing donors. All five reading failures found on 2026-09-25 were visible this way on the day they were made, and none was noticed, because the rows were published without the check. Reconcile before you publish; where it fails, ask a person.
tables.hazards:
FOUR HAZARDS, all found by Arthur's review of 2026-09-25 and all invisible to a whole-document text test.
  1. A CONTINUATION PAGE. The schedule runs onto a sheet the reader never opens. Green 2023's is numbered 'Page: 6.1' and carries the NINE largest donations in the return ($546,222.92). NZ First 2024's says so on its own face — 'Page added at the request of the Electoral commision due to space constraints in date feild of main form'. Look for a printed page label with a decimal, and for a sheet between two consecutively numbered pages.
  2. A CONTINUATION PAGE IS NOT A SCHEDULE. NZ First 2024's inserted sheet is a DATE BREAKDOWN whose last column is 'Donor Total' — the same figure already on the main form. Read as a schedule it produces duplicate donations; the reader took four of its detail lines as the donors' amounts and lost $89,921.04.
  3. AN AUDITOR'S STAMP OVER A FIGURE. Labour 2020 row 11 is $40,020.00 printed under Grant Thornton's circular 'Marked for identification purposes', and came back as $460.00. The stamp sits bottom-right, which is the AMOUNT column of the last row on the page — so the last row of each page of a stamped return is the one to check.
  4. A TWO-COLUMN DONOR CELL. Some forms put the donor's NAME and their STREET ADDRESS in separate table columns under one 'Donor's name and street address' heading. Green 2023 does, and the reader took the address column: 49 rows reading '<a donor's street address>' where a person's name belongs. If every donor in a part looks like an address, you are one column to the right.

prompt: This is a New Zealand Electoral Commission party donations and loans return. The DECLARATION page states Parts A, C, D, F and G and a grand total. Part A itemises donations above the disclosure threshold and is the ONLY part carrying donor names; Part G is the aggregate of everything under it and Part F is donations protected from disclosure by law, so neither names anybody — money sitting only in those parts is UNATTRIBUTED, not missing. Figures are often typed with no dollar sign and no cents (15,983), and NIL is written for zero; a declared NIL is a COMPLETE return, not a missing one. The threshold printed on a line ('of more than $1,500') is the FORM'S text and never the filed amount. Three versions of the grand total exist: (A+C+D+F+G) current with B excluded, (A+C+D+E) intermediate, and (A+B+C+D+E) on the 2019 form where B is anonymous donations and IS summed. Donor schedule pages print 'TOTAL FOR PART <X>' at the foot of each part's own table, which is a check on the declaration page.
notes:
9 of the eight parties' 56 live returns are this shape. A scan that yields nothing is recorded UNPARSED and the page says so; a second-rate figure published as a party's declared total is worse than an honest gap.

A scan cannot hide a two-column donor cell or a continuation page — it hides everything equally — so the hazards below matter here most, and the reconciliation check is the only thing that will tell you.

applies_to: A registered promoter's return of election expenses — a third party, neither party nor candidate, that spent over $100,000 on election advertising (Electoral Act 1993 s 206ZC). 20 of 21 held for 2020 and 2023.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --promoters (the Commission's expense page, which STATES each figure)

config.pages: every page, the longest held return being 8

process: The Commission's own expense page states every figure, so the document read has a gate before it is taken.
The SCHEDULE's `TOTAL FOR PART X` beats the DECLARATION block where both read: the schedule total is the figure the itemised rows add to.
Eleven of the twenty held returns have no text layer and are read by the recogniser; the reading is cached by sha256, never by filename.
gates: THE THREE HEADS OF 2020 ARE NOT ADDITIVE AND ARE NEVER SUMMED ACROSS A ROW. The form counts an advertisement that is both an election and a referendum advertisement IN FULL under each head. Family First declared $141,224.34 under Parts A, B and C and spent it once; a row sum publishes $423,673.02 that nobody spent.
PART A IS THE PUBLISHED FIGURE. It is money spent to influence a vote for a party or candidate. Referendum advertising bought a referendum result and is carried beside it, never inside it.
2023 RAN NO REFERENDUM, so its Parts B and C are NULL and not 0.00 — the head did not exist, which is a different statement from declaring nothing under it.

A FIGURE IS NOT ALWAYS BESIDE ITS LABEL, and on this form family it is the normal case. These are fillable PDFs: the value a filer types lands where the WIDGET sits, which is not the line the label prints on. Make It Legal's Part B total prints three lines above `TOTAL FOR PART B`; Diana Burgess's candidate total prints on the line `Write 'NIL' if you have NO expenses to declare`. A same-line rule reads both returns as declaring nothing, and the second one PASSED the form's own arithmetic because the parts it did find were 0 and 0 + 0 makes 0.

The form's printed THRESHOLD ($100,000 to file) and CAP are blanked before a line is searched for money. The Public Service Association's NIL return read $100,000 under all three heads, consistent with itself, until they were.
NIL IS A FIGURE and an empty cell is not one. The Commission writes Nil; a blank cell holds nothing to read.
on_fail: The Commission's stated figure loads and `stated_*` stays NULL with the reason. A promoter whose return is not held at all (The Better NZ Trust, 403 twice, ledgered) still carries the Commission's figure, because dropping a figure for want of its document is how 56 donation returns went missing.

by: gazette session 2, step 4.1 (appended by the integrator at gazette-2)
title: A notice prohibiting a person from managing companies (Gazette notice: Companies Act 1993 s 382, 383, 385; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 banning order)

landmarks: the title 'Notice Prohibiting (a) Person(s) …' together with, or the body alone holding, operative words ('hereby prohibit', 'is (permanently) prohibited', 'must not', 'banning order', 'made an order on', 'hereby revokes') under the Companies Act 1993 or the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, with the management words ('director or promoter', 'concerned in', 'taking part', 'management of') or a revocation; a body-only match needs a 'To:' field

signals_note: 'Hereby prohibit' alone is not this profile: under section go it also prohibits a doctor's prescribing, a vaccine's import and a fishing method. The Act and the management words are both required.
notes: One template since 2001, mostly section ot (a few go and gn): 'Pursuant to Section 385 of the Companies Act 1993 To: <name>. Of: <address>. Pursuant to section 385(1) …, I, <officer>, Deputy Registrar of Companies, hereby prohibit <name> from being a director or promoter of … for a period of <years and months> as from the date of this notice. Dated at <place> this <n>th (day) of <Month> <year>.' The capture runs fields together ('Smith.Of:', 'ofthis'). Six actions from the operative words: prohibition (the Registrar's, s 385), court order (the Registrar gives notice of a court's order, s 382 and 383, sometimes permanent), banning order (FMC Act; may name two people, two 'To:' fields), variation (a court set aside the Registrar's term; names the notice varied), substitution (a prohibition with a note revoking an earlier notice, named), revocation (revokes a named notice and prohibits nobody; one was revoked 'as published in error' because it named the wrong person, so a revocation's text is never read for a name and the revoked notice's person is not published). The 'Of:' field (or 'Formerly of:') is an address, often a home: private (hard limit 15). An alias in brackets is kept apart from the name. The name is printed twice; both are compared.
applies_to: 537 notices, 2001 to 2026 (535 section ot)
process: Decide the action from the operative words.
Take each 'To:' to 'Of:' as one person; the address to the private schema.
Read the Act and section, the term in months or 'permanently', the start (stated, or the date of the notice), the 'Dated' day, and the notices acted on.
Mark the rows of a notice that a later one revokes, replaces or varies.
gates: Every recognised notice gives a person, is a revocation, or is a catch-log line.
A revocation, substitution or variation names the notice it acts on, and that notice is held.
on_fail: set aside the person or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 2, step 4.1 (appended by the integrator at gazette-2)
title: A notice of a liquidator's appointment, and the Official Assignee's list of liquidations (Gazette section al)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code al in the notice number (<year>-al<n>): every notice so filed, and no other

signals_note: Recognised by the Gazette's classification, never by title words: 'Appointment of …' under go, vr and au is a public office, and 'liquidator' also appears under ds, ar and md.
notes: Two shapes. notice: the companies named in the title ('ACME LIMITED (in liquidation)'; the capture can carry a long title's end into the text before 'Notice of'; a title of only 'Appointment of Liquidator' names them in the body, often as 'on the dates and times below: 9 May 2016 ACME LIMITED at 10.30am.'), the operative sentence, a claims date, often 'Dated', the signature ('Ann Example and Bob Sample, Joint Liquidators', printed in capitals or with initials), then business contact lines that are never read. list: the Official Assignee's 'Liquidations', 'NAME LIMITED | 9 May 2022' repeated, or before about 2016 a date and then the names liquidated that day, each ending in its suffix and a stop. A title is cut into companies at ', ' and ' and ' only where each part ends in a legal suffix (LIMITED, LTD, INCORPORATED, PARTNERSHIP, TRUST), so 'SMITH AND JONES LIMITED' stays one company; a part with no suffix is a catch-log line. Who appointed: section 241(2)(a) shareholders, (b) board, (c) court where cited, else the notice's words. The date is the one the notice prints near its operative words (with its time), or each company's own in the 'below' layout; a notice whose several dates cannot be placed gives none. Liquidators from the signature (checked against the text above it: full name, surname only as when initials sign, or no), else from the operative sentence; a post-nominal (C.A., FCA) is not a person. No address, telephone or email is read: a director acting as liquidator may print a home address.
process: Decide the shape.
Read the companies (title, carried-over title, body, or list rows).
Read who appointed, the statute, the date and time per company, the Dated day, the company number where one company prints one.
Read the liquidators from the signature, else the operative sentence.
gates: Every al notice gives a company or is a catch-log line.
Every title part, list row or signature the reader cannot place is a catch-log line, never a guess.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

signals_note: Captured and read off-estate by the provider (ruling 78). The split is the estate's own, deterministic (registers/hansard/split.py, rule `hansard-day split 1`): headings are the centred lines (capitals from indent 1, mixed case centred within 10 of the page's middle), a section is the text under one run of heading lines, a turn is a paragraph opening `NAME (role or Party—Electorate) [(hh:mm)] [to the Minister …]:` in capitals, a role, or a mixed-case name seen in capitals that day or held by the old roster. Proved on the 137 days both sources hold (hansard-3): the split finds more member turns than the old speaker lists on 129 days (the old lists skip the question line and most debate speakers) and fewer on the 8 urgency sittings whose later calendar days the MCP lacks.
prompt:
You read one piece of a New Zealand parliamentary debate (Hansard): speeches by members, each opening with the speaker's name in capitals or a role such as SPEAKER, then what they said. Answer with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"summary": "<one sentence, at most 40 words, saying what this piece of the debate is about, naming nobody>",
 "names": [{"name": "<a person or body named in the speeches, exactly as printed>", "kind": "person" | "company" | "agency" | "body" | "other", "role": "<the role the text gives them, in the text's own words, e.g. Minister of Finance, chief executive, constituent, former member, the applicant; null when none>", "of": "<for a person: the organisation the text says they are of or from, as printed; otherwise null>"}]}
Rules. List every person, company, government agency or department, council, court, iwi, trust, union, charity and other body that a speaker NAMES in a speech, each once. Do not list the speakers themselves (the names that open a paragraph before a colon) unless another speaker names them in a speech. A company or incorporated business is kind company; a ministry, department, Crown entity, council, police or court is kind agency; any other organisation is kind body; a named individual is kind person; use other when the kind cannot be told. Keep spelling, initials and honorifics as printed; never expand an initial; never add an address, an age or any fact the text does not state; never name anyone the text does not name. A role or party alone ("the Minister", "National") is not a name.
notes: The reader's budget is 40,000 characters of speech a request: the text-reader profile's context is 16,384 tokens, the answer 4,096, the prompt about 420, and Hansard English measured at about 4.3 characters a token (31 October 2026). A day is read in pieces: one per section within the budget; a section over it cut at speaker turns, then paragraphs, then lines, each part within the budget; a piece's reading stored at page p under the day's hash, the pieces joined into one reading at page 1 (settings `joined`). The speakers are the turns' own rows and are not asked for.

process: Recognise the layout by its page furniture; drop the furniture, the cover, contents and index.
Headings to sections, speaker lines to turns, the member matched to the old roster within the day's Parliament; the counts into `days`, the rows into `day_sections` and `day_turns` (no model).
The text reader over every piece within the budget; the readings joined under the day's hash; the load picks the names into `people` and `pub.hansard_people`; never a link, never a claim.
gates: Every day split or set aside at stage read with the reason (no pages, no body page).
Every piece within the budget, or the day set aside naming the piece.
One reading per piece and one joined reading per day hash; a reading under another profile version fails the check.
Every name row cites the day's record, piece and ordinal.
on_fail: set aside at read; the check fails
